Not for redistribution without written consent of Morgan Stanley Morgan Stanley RESEARCH Idea February 4, 2026 08:11 PM GMT AppLovin Corp | North America CloudX and META and Genie, Oh My APP shares have derated to 15x '27 EBITDA on fresh worries about disruption to the industry. We analyze three key investor concerns on CloudX, META, and Genie that have arisen in recent days. While these are real concerns, the magnitude of derating may also be creating an opportunity. Remain OW. Key Takeaways APP shares have fallen on fresh worries about disruption to mobile ad tech and video games, with APP now trading at ~15x '27 EBITDA for 31% EBITDA growth We analyze three key investor concerns, 1) the launch of CloudX’s mediation, which we see as misunderstood and only a minor competitive threat 2) META making a renewed push in APP's market (a genuine concern), though we see limited evidence that a push is coming in the near-term 3) World models like Genie, which remain a key debate for the game industry but we do not expect to fundamentally impact pure-play ad techs like APP In our view, the magnitude of the derating may be creating an opportunity similar to APP's selloff to $219 in April '25 APP Has Sold Off On Three Main Investor Concerns, Creating a Potential Opportunity as Shares Now Trade at ~15x '27 EBITDA: APP shares have fallen 30% since 1/29, as a series of new and resurgent investor concerns have taken center stage. All of them focus on potential disruption to mobile ad tech, the video game industry, or both and we address each in turn below. As we noted in World Models Are Here...So What Do They Mean for U, RBLX, TTWO and APP?, these disruption narratives can weigh on multiples over long periods and that has been evident across Internet (e.g. GOOGL and ride share) as well as much of software Software. That said, with APP now trading at ~15x our '27 EBITDA for 31% '25-'28 EBITDA growth, we think ad tech's best executor is priced for significant risks, some of which are more salient than others. We fully acknowledge that the market may now assign a lower multiple to APP (and its peers). However, the magnitude of the derating may ultimately create a moment of opportunity...much as it did when APP touched $219 per share in April of '25. We also note that none of these concerns are idiosyncratic to APP. From META's perspective, we view the opportunity to re-enter the ~$80bn in-app ad market as a clear call option. We believe the Meta Audience Network footprint remains small for 3P in-app today, but that growing demand for ecommerce (and other performance) advertising in the channel could make it a more attractive opportunity going forward. So What Factors is the Market Debating on APP?

1) The GA Launch of CloudX Increasing Competition in Mediation: A
misunderstood catalyst, with limited negative implications for APP and the space.
• What Happened? On 2/4, independent ad tech company CloudX launched a new mobile mediation product that competes directly with other leading players including APP's MAX, U's LevelPlay, and GOOGL's AdMob.
Our View: While CloudX is launching its new tool with demand from META on day 1, that is fundamentally distinct from a broader push to scale Meta Audience Network's in-game campaigns. CloudX is an independent ad tech that will solicit demand from any source to fill its ad inventory, including but not limited to META. Even if CloudX gains traction, it constitutes a modest competitive threat in mediation from a new entrant. Meta Audience Network's broader plans are a separate issue, which brings us to factor #2.
2) The Risk of a Renewed Push from Meta Audience Network Increasing Competition Among DSPs: A genuine concern, but with limited evidence of a nearterm launch.
• What Happened? On 1/29, a mobile game industry consultant reported data from "dozens of clients" showing that META gaining significant share in ingame advertising on iOS. This contributed to APP's underperformance on 1/30.
Our View: META was previously the largest player in in-game ads on iOS, before AAPL's user privacy changes in '21 cut Meta Audience Network off from its primary targeting data. Since then, debate has persisted on whether META planned to innovate around the new constraints to reclaim market share. This remains a material risk, given the resources at META's disposal. That said, the evidence appears to be limited to a single blog post. We are unconvinced that a battle for in-game ad market share is imminent and remain constructive on APP's moats (e.g. scale, data, and supply-side footprint).
3) The Genie 3 Launch Disrupting the Game Industry By Changing How Games Are Made: An important long-term debate for video game companies, but one that we do not expect to materially impact ad tech.
• What Happened? On 1/29, GOOGL announced it was rolling out its Genie 3 world model for subscribers to test. This hands-on experience raised concerns that world models could disrupt how video games are produced, negatively impacting gaming (and gaming-adjacent) stocks on 1/30.
Our View: As we wrote in our deep dive (see here), this remains an important debate for video game publishers and toolmakers. That said, we expect that games will continue monetizing their ad inventory and spending on paid user acquisition, irrespective of what software tools they use to produce their games. The need to participate in advertising would also apply equally to incumbents and new entrants. With that in mind, we do not expect world models like GOOGL's Genie to have a fundamental impact on pure-play ad techs like APP.
